To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The hard QCD contribution to the ϱ -trajectory is weakly coupled, 2) The hard QED contribution to the ρ -trajectory is weak and can be neglected, and 3) The Reggeon trajectory is a sum over all hard QCD and hard QED contributions.
the hard part of the Reggeon trajectory α ϱ ( − t ) is weakly coupled at all − t and that the soft part of α ϱ ( -t) is strongly coupled.

the effective ρ trajectory becomes negative at s ≅ − t ≅ 8 GeV2, but the hard QCD trajectory becomes negative only at s ≅ ( − t ) ≅ 10 4 GeV2, and that the Reggeons in the reaction π−p→π0X are the same as the Reggeons that govern π−p→η′X.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of hard exclusive and inclusive reactions involving mesons in the t - channel.
the study of Reggeon trajectories in the large momentum transfer region.
the study of hard exclusive reactions and the study of the asymptotic behavior of Reggeon trajectories in large momentum transfer inclusive reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Reggeons trajectories are weakly coupled at high energy.
the Reggeons are a weakly interacting system of quark-antipair and that their contribution to mesonic exchange reactions is a calculable perturbation of QCD.
the Reggeons are not a fundamental feature of QCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Reggeon trajectories can be studied in perturbatively QCD.
perturbative QED is not a good approximation to QED in the infrared region and perturbative QFT is not a good approximaton to QFT in the infrared region.
the hard QED and QCD parts of the Reggeon trajectory are weakly coupled and their contributions are hidden until very large energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Reggeeon trajectory is not a fundamental concept of QCD, rather it is a consequence of the fact that the quark-antquark exchange amplitude is a perturbative QED process.
the Reggeeon trajectory α ( t ) = α 0 + α 1 t + α 2 t 2 + ⋯, with α 1 = 0, is not a good description of mesonic exchange hadronic reactions at high energy.
the Reggion contributions are not hidden by the hard QCD contributions in the large momentum transfer reactions and that the Reggeons can be studied in a perturbative way in such reactions.
